holidays.name: National Tequila Day
holidays.description: Raise a glass (responsibly!) to the blue agave spirit that gives us margaritas, palomas, and sunrise cocktails. It's a day for sipping, mixing, and learning the difference between a blanco and an añejo.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that has grown through food-and-drink calendars and social media. Its roots trace to tequila's home in Jalisco, Mexico, where the spirit is named after the town of Tequila.
holidays.funFact: True tequila can only be made from blue Weber agave, and the plant can take around 7 to 10 years to mature before harvest.

holidays.name: National Drive-Thru Day
holidays.description: A salute to the glorious invention that lets you order a burger without ever leaving your car or putting on real pants. Celebrate by rolling up to your favorite window and shouting your order into a speaker.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance, often linked to In-N-Out Burger, which opened its first drive-thru stand in Baldwin Park, California, in 1948.
holidays.funFact: In-N-Out's original drive-thru was one of the first in California to use a two-way speaker box, so customers could order without a carhop.

holidays.name: National Cousins Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the built-in partners in crime who share your grandparents, your embarrassing childhood stories, and probably your weird laugh. Call, text, or plan a reunion with your favorite cousin.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance of unclear origin, widely shared on holiday calendars and social media as a day to honor extended family.
holidays.funFact: Cousins are sometimes described by degree and removal. A first cousin once removed is the child of your first cousin, so family trees can get delightfully tangled.
